sections.h2: What makes selling quickly in New Bern different from other coastal towns?
sections.html:
Two rivers meet at New Bern, and an old core sits beside newer subdivisions. That mix shapes what a quick sale looks like. Owners of historic or storm-worn houses often hit snags with lenders and inspectors, which is why many look at cash buyers who skip that process.

The Census Bureau puts New Bern at 34,724 people for July 1, 2025, about 3,400 more than its April 2020 estimates base of 31,319. Within the 28.42 square miles of land, density is roughly 1,101 people per square mile. The 2010 census counted 29,524, so the city has added residents in each count since.

The Craven County seat has an unusually older population: 24.5% of residents are 65 or over, and veterans number 3,524. Both facts feed the sale pool. Heirs with a parent's house to clear, and retirees leaving for a family member's town, are common sellers, and each needs a firm closing day.

  • A retail listing fits a house in sound shape when the seller can sit through a buyer's loan process.
  • A cash sale fits a house with needed repairs, a renter inside or a date that cannot move.
  • Selling without an agent suits owners at ease with disclosure forms and contract drafting.

sections.h2: How are New Bern homes valued and rented?
sections.html:
Homes that owners live in are worth a median of $240,100 in New Bern over 2020 to 2024, and 59.7% of the city's homes are owner-lived. These are citywide, so a downtown cottage or a house by the water will sit off the median.

The 18.8-minute commute is short, which suits a compact town. Roughly 85 of every 100 residents had not moved in the past year, at 84.6%. Monthly costs of ownership run $1,504 with a mortgage and $567 without, so carrying an empty house for months is a cost worth counting before you decide how long to wait.

sections.h2: Do historic district rules in New Bern affect a sale?
sections.html:
Yes, if the house is in a historic district. The city requires a Certificate of Appropriateness before any exterior alteration there, and buyers who plan visible changes will need to apply.

City staff can sign off on some work classed as in-kind replacement or minor, while the rest goes before the Historic Preservation Commission. The commission works from the Land Use Ordinance and its Historic District Guidelines, both linked from the city's HPC page, which also lists an application, instructions and a worksheet.

A weather note sits on that page too: it calls old buildings in low, coastal ground hard to keep up through severe storms and links a state preservation office video on getting ready and recovering. A listing that discloses the district and any past storm damage reads as straightforward to buyers.

  • Learn whether the parcel is mapped into a district before you set the price.
  • Mention the review requirement to buyers early.
  • Skip costly exterior repairs if you plan an as-is sale.

sections.h2: How does Craven County handle revaluation and the tax bill?
sections.html:
Craven County appraises the parcel, and its tax department says a countywide revaluation for tax year 2028 is under way. The previous one was finished in 2023.

For a seller, the 2028 revaluation is mostly a talking point with buyers. The county's page says a comparable sales search will open in February 2028. Until then, the tax department can give you the property card for your parcel.

Statewide rules fill in the rest. The statewide pattern is a September 1 due date, no interest into early January, then a 2% charge, then three-quarters of a percent monthly from February. A value dispute goes first to the county's review board, and a further appeal to the Property Tax Commission has a 30-day window after the board mails its ruling.

Your closing attorney sets how the year's bill is split with the buyer.

sections.h2: What does New Bern's economy mean for buyers of a house here?
sections.html:
Medical services lead the local numbers. In 2022, clinics, hospitals and social services took in $895,063,000, against $1,323,049,000 in retail sales, or $41,980 per resident. Hotels and restaurants took in $180,697,000.

Education and connectivity shape who buys. High school diplomas cover 92.8% of adults past 25, and 29.4% have a four-year degree. A computer sits in 93.7% of households and 85.9% pay for broadband, so remote workers can consider the area. The labor force share is 57.2%, lower than in many cities because so many residents are retired.

Poverty stands at 17.3%, and 9.2% of residents under 65 lack health insurance. For a seller these numbers say that a good share of local buyers rely on modest budgets, so a clean, fairly priced house sells faster than a stretch price.

Per capita income is $38,196, and 10.9% of residents under 65 live with a disability. Another 5.8% of residents were born abroad. Children under 18 are 22.4% of the population.

sections.h2: Which fees come with recording a New Bern deed?
sections.html:
Sellers pay the state's deed tax, $1 for each $500 of price, before recording; filing starts at $26.00 for a general instrument. Recording a release of a paid-off deed of trust carries no fee.

Your closing attorney handles these payments. Ask the Craven County register for office hours.

sections.h2: Which New Bern owners may hold a tax exclusion that ends with a sale?
sections.html:
Older owners and veterans are a large part of the city, so this question comes up often. The Census Bureau counts 3,524 veterans in New Bern, and 24.5% of residents are 65 or older.

  • Seniors or disabled owners within the income cap can exclude the larger of $25,000 or half the appraised value; the state printed a $38,800 cap for 2026.
  • Disabled veterans can exclude the first $45,000 of appraised value, with no age or income test on the state form.
  • A circuit breaker caps the tax at a share of income and defers the rest as a lien.

Each owner may use only one program. When the house is sold, deferred circuit breaker taxes for the last three fiscal years come due, so have the Craven County assessor give you a figure ahead of closing.

sections.h2: What should a New Bern owner facing foreclosure know?
sections.html: The Craven County clerk of court hears foreclosures for New Bern houses. Once an auction sale is reported, ten-day periods open for higher bids. An owner who pays the loan off beforehand keeps any equity, so request a payoff figure and the case file first.

sections.h2: What are the first steps to take now?
sections.html:
Gather the deed, a loan payoff letter and the last tax bill, then set your latest acceptable closing date.

  • Confirm the district status of the address.
  • Walk the house and note roof, moisture and foundation concerns.
  • Request a few written offers and compare the amount each leaves after costs.
  • Ask the assessor if a homestead exclusion on the parcel ends at sale.

The county offices can confirm what applies to your parcel.

faqs.q: Can I sell a New Bern house with storm damage?
faqs.a: Yes. Cash buyers purchase damaged houses as they stand, and a retail listing works if you disclose the damage and expect credit requests.

faqs.q: Does New Bern require approval for exterior work in a historic district?
faqs.a: Yes for exterior changes. A Certificate of Appropriateness is required, though staff can clear minor work.

faqs.q: Who pays the deed excise tax in Craven County?
faqs.a: The seller. The statute puts it on the transferor, at $1 per $500.

faqs.q: When does Craven County revalue next?
faqs.a: Tax year 2028 is the one the county tax department names. The last was completed in 2023.

faqs.q: Can selling stop a foreclosure in New Bern?
faqs.a: Paying the loan off before the auction ends it. After an auction, upset bids can still arrive for ten days, so ask the clerk first.
